answer: Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. A ripple of per-task receipts records who did what, and the velvet of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, held in escrow until finality, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Reaching the island of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
